source.title: Pattern separation in the human hippocampal CA3 and dentate gyrus

confidence_rationale: High-resolution human fMRI dissociating a strong pattern-separation bias localized to CA3/dentate gyrus from a pattern-completion bias in CA1/subiculum/entorhinal/parahippocampal cortex. Strong, human, anatomically specific evidence that the DG performs the separation operation REE plans as MECH-147. Held below 0.85 because fMRI infers the computation from a repetition-suppression signature rather than recording sparse codes directly, and the candidate gate is about the POLICY over separation, of which DG separation is only the separate-pole effector.
failure_signatures: fMRI shows a separation-vs-completion bias by region but does not record the sparse orthogonalized codes directly; the DG sparse-encoding mechanism is inferred, not observed at single-trace resolution.
Demonstrates the separation EFFECTOR (DG) but not a control policy deciding WHEN to separate vs integrate -- supports MECH-147 (substrate) more than the allocation-gate policy.

Pattern completion in CA1/EC means the same circuit that separates also actively re-integrates; a REE design that builds separation without the complementary completion/integration pole would mis-model the system.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In humans, high-resolution fMRI during incidental encoding of similar (lure) and repeated stimuli shows a strong bias toward pattern separation confined to the CA3/dentate gyrus, while CA1, subiculum, entorhinal and parahippocampal cortices show a bias toward pattern completion.
mapping.ree_translation: Empirical, human-anatomical backing for the separate-pole of the allocation gate and specifically for REE's planned MECH-147 (DG sparse, non-redundant encoding of similar z_world before rollout). The DG/CA3 separation-vs-completion dissociation is the substrate over which a Contextual Memory Allocation Gate would arbitrate: separation = allocate a fresh trace; completion/integration = reuse an existing one. Confirms that separation is a dedicated, regionally specialized operation rather than a side effect of failed retrieval.
mapping.mapping_caveat: fMRI infers the separation/completion computation from a repetition-suppression contrast, not from direct observation of sparse codes; the mapping to a discrete REE z_world orthogonalization is by analogy. This paper supports the EXISTENCE and localization of the separation effector (MECH-147), not the control policy that decides when to engage it -- the gate's novelty lies in the latter.
mapping.source_context: Human; high-resolution fMRI of medial temporal lobe subfields during an incidental encoding task with novel, repeated, and similar-lure stimuli.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (Science, human, subfield-resolved fMRI, foundational). Mapping fidelity high to MECH-147 (DG separation substrate); lower to the allocation-gate policy. Transfer risk low (human data; the cross-domain step is to a computational z_world code, which is conceptually close to the orthogonalization the DG is modelled to perform).
